one_line: The video demonstrates how chin augmentation alters the perception of nose size using a split-screen comparison and an interactive physical exercise.

hook.what_happens: A split-screen comparison of a woman's face asks if her nose is too big, then reveals it is the same nose in both images.
hook.why_it_works: It challenges the viewer's visual perception immediately, creating curiosity about the optical illusion.

shots.description: Split-screen comparison of a woman's face labeled 'Before' and 'After' with a sliding transition line.
Heatmap overlay showing pixel changes, accompanied by a bar chart indicating where edits occurred.
Close-up of the face with circular annotations highlighting the relationship between the nose and chin.
A clean, minimalist list of instructions prompting the viewer to perform a physical action.
Side-by-side comparison of the original and edited face, showing the holistic effect of the change.
A minimalist call-to-action screen featuring a search bar typing out the brand name.

devices.name: sliding comparison line
devices.what_it_is: A vertical line that sweeps across the face to reveal the edited version.
devices.used_for: Highlighting subtle differences between before and after states.

devices.name: heatmap overlay
devices.what_it_is: A glowing color overlay indicating pixel-level changes on the face.
devices.used_for: Proving objectively where the image was modified.

devices.name: bar chart
devices.what_it_is: A simple bar graph showing percentage of pixel changes per facial region.
devices.used_for: Quantifying the visual data for scientific credibility.

devices.name: interactive search bar
devices.what_it_is: A simulated search input field that types out the brand name.
devices.used_for: Directing user search behavior for the CTA.

onscreen_text.text: Not one feature. The whole face.

transcript.text: Think your nose is too big?
Same woman, twice.
Same nose, both photographs.
But it looks smaller in the second.
Her chin is what moved.
Here is every pixel that changed.
Almost none of it is on her nose.
Your eye doesn't measure features.
It compares them.
When the chin sits back, the nose stands out.
Your brain calls it a big nose.
Bring it forward and the nose has something to sit against.
It didn't shrink. The face caught up.
Try it right now.
Push your lower jaw forward.
Your nose just got smaller. You didn't touch it.
The question was never which feature to fix.
It's what the whole face does when one thing moves.
See it on your own face first.
A preview, not a promise.
Search Refina AI.

narrative_arc: Introduce the optical illusion of nose size vs. chin position.
Provide data-driven proof that only the chin was modified.
Explain the psychological and visual science behind facial proportions.
Engage the viewer with an interactive physical test to prove the concept.
Conclude with a call to action to try the AI preview tool on their own face.

cta.what: Search 'Refina AI' to preview facial adjustments on your own face.

subjects: Unidentified woman (model demonstrating facial structure changes)
what_makes_it_work: The interactive 'Try it now' segment physically proves the visual theory to the viewer instantly.
Data visualization (heatmap and bar chart) adds scientific credibility to the visual claim.
Minimalist, clean aesthetic keeps the focus entirely on facial geometry and structure.
